title: Research Biotech Office Rates: Monthly Janitorial Spend Benchmarks for Biotech & Life Sciences Office Wings
seoTitle: Research Biotech Office Rates: Monthly Janitorial Spend Benchmarks
metaDescription: Research biotech office rates run $0.07-$0.12 per sq ft per visit for 10,000+ sq ft wings. See monthly benchmarks by size and test your budget in our tool.
excerpt: Biotech and life sciences office wings sit next to laboratories, which changes traffic patterns, restroom use, and the cleaning frequency that tenants and auditors expect. This guide benchmarks monthly janitorial spend by wing size and explains which factors push your quote up or down.
quickAnswer: Biotech office wings between 10,000 and 24,999 sq ft are typically quoted at $0.07 to $0.12 per sq ft per visit, so a 12,000 sq ft wing with mixed flooring cleaned five weekdays runs about $794 to $1,361 per visit, or roughly $17,186 to $29,461 per month. Smaller incubator suites cost more per square foot, and wings supporting round-the-clock lab shifts often need seven-day service.

blocks.text: What Counts as a Biotech Office Wing

This benchmark covers the non-laboratory side of a life sciences building: write-up desks, scientist and executive offices, conference rooms, breakrooms, restrooms, and the corridors that connect to lab suites. It does not cover cleanroom, vivarium, or BSL-2 lab housekeeping, which is priced on a completely different specialty basis. Many tenants make the mistake of sending one RFP for both; separating the office wing usually lowers the blended cost because standard janitorial crews can handle it at office rates with a few lab-adjacent protocols.

Even so, a biotech office wing is not a typical corporate floor. Scientists move between labs and desks dozens of times a day, sticky mats at lab doors need changing, glass partitions are everywhere, and many companies run lab shifts on weekends. Those factors shape both frequency and price.
Monthly Spend Benchmarks by Wing Size

Figures below apply the national per-visit brackets, the stated flooring multiplier, and the frequency multiplier. Monthly totals use 4.333 weeks per month: 8.66 visits for twice weekly, 13 for three times weekly, 21.65 for weekday daily, and 30.33 for seven-day service.

blocks.caption: Biotech and life sciences office wing cleaning benchmarks (national averages)

blocks.title: Per-square-foot monthly view
blocks.text: The 12,000 sq ft weekday-daily wing works out to about $1.43 to $2.46 per sq ft per month. Moving the same wing to seven-day service raises the monthly bill by about 35 percent even though the per-visit price drops slightly, because visits climb from 21.65 to 30.33.

Life sciences buildings are usually designed with restroom counts sized for lab occupancy, and office wings inherit that capacity. A 12,000 sq ft wing commonly has four to six restrooms plus locker or shower rooms used by lab staff who cycle to work or change out of lab clothing. Expect $15 to $30 per restroom per visit when the count exceeds the office norm; two extra restrooms at weekday daily service adds about $650 to $1,300 per month.

Breakrooms are another driver. Scientists eat at their desks less than office workers because food is banned in labs, so breakrooms and kitchenettes see heavy, concentrated use. Breakroom sanitation typically adds $12 to $25 per visit, and many biotech tenants need two or three kitchenettes per floor.

items: Lab-to-office transition zones see constant foot traffic. Adhesive sticky mats at lab doors should be peeled to a fresh layer daily or per shift, depending on the tenant's protocol.
VCT and sheet vinyl in corridors pick up cart-wheel marks from sample and supply carts; plan burnishing monthly and a quarterly deep floor program at $0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month.
Carpet tile at write-up desks collects more fine particulate than a standard office because of HVAC air changes and lab-coat lint; HEPA vacuuming is the norm.
Glass partitions and lab viewing windows add interior glass work at $15 to $35 per visit if included in every service.

blocks.text: Recommended Frequency for Biotech Office Wings

Most biotech office wings over 10,000 sq ft run weekday daily service for restrooms, breakrooms, trash, and high-touch surfaces, with vacuuming and full dusting rotating through the week. Companies running weekend lab shifts typically add a light weekend visit focused on restrooms, breakrooms, and trash rather than paying full seven-day rates. Small incubator suites can often succeed at two or three visits per week, provided the incubator's shared restrooms and kitchens are handled by the building operator.

Because office wings share air handling and corridors with labs, EHS teams often ask that vacuums meet true HEPA filtration. The Atrix VACBP1 Ergo is rated HEPA 99.97 percent with an 8-quart capacity at 10.3 lb, giving long runs between bag changes in a large wing. The Powr-Flite BP6S Comfort Pro uses five-stage HEPA filtration in a 6-quart, 11 lb package and runs at 62 dBA, quiet enough to work near scientists finishing late analyses. The Hoover Commercial C2401 Shoulder Vac Pro, with a 6.4-quart HEPA media bag at 9.2 lb, suits quick passes in conference rooms and incubator suites. Ask bidders to document filter change intervals as part of their quality plan.

blocks.title: Split the RFP
blocks.text: Bid office-wing janitorial separately from lab housekeeping and glass-wash support. Office crews at $35 to $65 per hour can handle the wing, while lab-trained technicians at $55 to $95 per hour should be reserved for areas that actually require gowning and lab-specific SOPs.
Budgeting Steps for Facilities and Workplace Teams

items.name: Map the boundary
items.text: Mark exactly where the office wing ends and lab suites begin, including which transition doors and sticky mats the janitorial crew owns.

items.name: Count restrooms, showers, and kitchenettes
items.text: These drive the largest adders and should be listed with fixture counts.

items.name: Choose a frequency by zone
items.text: Daily for restrooms and breakrooms, rotating for desk dusting and vacuuming, and weekend light service if lab shifts run.

items.name: Model the monthly figure
items.text: Multiply per-visit price by visits per month using 4.333 weeks, then add the amortized deep floor program.

items.name: Benchmark bids
items.text: Compare each bid to the per-square-foot ranges above and ask for line-item detail where a quote sits outside them.

blocks.text: Enter your wing's square footage, flooring, restroom count, and frequency into the Office Cleaning Cost Calculator, then compare incoming bids in the Quote Comparator before your next renewal.

faqs.q: What are typical research biotech office rates per square foot?
faqs.a: National averages run $0.12 to $0.20 per sq ft per visit for suites under 2,500 sq ft, $0.09 to $0.15 for 2,500 to 9,999 sq ft, $0.07 to $0.12 for 10,000 to 24,999 sq ft, and $0.05 to $0.10 above 25,000 sq ft, before flooring, frequency, and add-on adjustments.

faqs.q: Does the office wing cleaning contract cover the labs?
faqs.a: It should not by default. Lab housekeeping, cleanroom cleaning, vivarium care, and anything requiring gowning or lab-specific SOPs belong in a separate specialty scope. The office wing contract should state which transition zones and sticky mats the crew maintains and that crews do not enter posted lab areas.

faqs.q: How is monthly cost calculated for weekday daily service?
faqs.a: Weekday daily service equals 5 visits times 4.333 weeks, or 21.65 visits per month. A 12,000 sq ft wing quoted at $794 to $1,361 per visit therefore runs about $17,186 to $29,461 per month before restroom surcharges, consumables, or the deep floor program.

faqs.q: What insurance should a biotech tenant require from its janitorial vendor?
faqs.a: Require a COI with general liability of at least $1 million per occurrence and $2 million aggregate, statutory workers' compensation, umbrella coverage often of $5 million for life sciences landlords, and a fidelity bond. Many lab landlords also require pollution liability if the vendor handles anything beyond ordinary office waste.

faqs.q: Should biotech office wings use green cleaning products?
faqs.a: Yes, for routine surfaces and floors. Green Seal GS-37 or EPA Safer Choice products reduce volatile organic compounds that can interfere with sensitive instruments and indoor air quality targets, while EPA-registered disinfectants remain appropriate for restrooms, breakrooms, and high-touch points.
